study type: Retrospective cohort study (secondary analysis of a registry)
outcome: Composite of postpartum infection (endometritis, sepsis, pelvic abscess, urinary tract infection, necrotizing fasciitis, septic pelvic thrombophlebitis)
cohort: The study included 559 women who experienced chorioamnionitis in labor and successfully delivered vaginally after a previous cesarean section.
finding: Approximately 5% of women with chorioamnionitis who had a successful VBAC experienced a postpartum infectious complication, with higher rates observed in those delivering at <32 weeks and with prepregnancy BMI >=40, while receipt of postpartum antibiotics significantly decreased the odds of infection.
mod_finding: The study focused on identifying risk factors for postpartum infectious complications specifically following a successful vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) in women with chorioamnionitis.
